source.title: Overparametrization of HyperNetworks at Fixed FLOP-Count Enables Fast Neural Image Enhancement

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures test error across model-size settings to test for double descent, using an image-enhancement task and HyperConvolution networks rather than reproducing the original experiments.
record.gate_note: The ZRR parameter-count sweep and its standard-convolution comparison bear on V1. The cited results from other work, and the ZRR/SIDD benchmark comparisons in Tables 1 and 2, are not parameter-sweep results and are not recorded as rows. FLOP counts are not test-error outcomes for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps parameter count by widening the HyperConvolution MLPs in a UNet-like image-enhancement network. It plots ZRR test error (1-MS-SSIM) against parameter count and calls the curve double-descent-consistent. This is a model-wise test of V1 in a new setting (image-to-image regression, hypernetwork parameters at fixed FLOPs), so T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that enlarging the HyperConvolution MLPs raises parameter count at negligible FLOP cost and lowers test error along a curve they call double-descent-consistent. They add that at equal FLOPs this beats standard convolutions, and that a very narrow forward network underperforms despite many parameters, possibly due to an information bottleneck. Their broader conclusion is that extra parameters can improve generalization without extra compute.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies HyperConvolution MLP size in an image-enhancement UNet-like network and evaluates ZRR test error at near-constant FLOPs; it does not reproduce the original study's settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported parameter-count generalization result is for HyperConvolutions; the standard-convolution comparison is presented separately, and its curve shape is not described in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: A network with a very narrow forward path (nfwd=8, nhid=4000, 113M params) underperforms wider networks with fewer parameters (e.g. MS-SSIM 0.8428 vs 0.8617 at 90M). The authors suggest an information bottleneck.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Raw parameter count added via hypernetwork MLPs does not by itself determine generalization; forward-network width limits the benefit of overparameterization.

record.code_released: not stated; key code functions are included in the appendix
record.peer_reviewed: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: The double-descent result is described qualitatively and shown in a figure without exact curve values or stated uncertainty. The study does not report whether the peak is at the training-set fitting threshold.
record.rows_left_out: No other parameter-count test-error sweep results are reported. Benchmark comparisons in Tables 1 and 2 do not vary model size as a sweep and were excluded.

untested.parts: Whether the test-error peak sits at the size that just fits the training set (no training error reported). Whether standard-convolution width scaling shows double descent (R2 not described).

missing.what: Numeric test-error values along the MLP-size sweep, and the tested nhid values, needed to locate any peak
Training error along the sweep, needed to identify the interpolation threshold

record.verdict_notes: The paper treats double descent mainly as 'more parameters generalize better' (Sec. 3.1, Fig. 2 cartoon). It does not demonstrate an error peak near interpolation, so the V1 support is weak and qualitative. No label noise, epoch-wise or sample-wise analyses are run. Tables 1–2 are benchmark comparisons, correctly excluded from rows.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish whether the peak coincides with the model size that just fits the training set.

rows.subject: UNet-like architecture with HyperConvolutions
rows.size_stated: Number of MLP units varied; exact tested values not stated in text
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of hidden units in the HyperConvolution MLPs and measured test error against parameter count.

conditions.value: fixed in the large-image limit; negligible increase reported

rows.measure: Test error (1-MS-SSIM) as a function of parameter count
rows.value: The authors report a generalization curve consistent with double descent as the number of MLP units increases.
rows.note: The text describes the curve but does not give exact curve values or establish where its peak lies relative to fitting the training set.
rows.check: The state rests only on the authors' wording ('consistent with double-descent generalization'). The extracted text cannot show whether Fig. 3 has a visible peak; its y-axis spans about 0.154–0.166 over 10^6–10^7 parameters. No training error is reported, so no interpolation threshold is identified. Parameters grow only in the hypernetwork MLP (nfwd=8, nembed=8 fixed), not in the forward network. Hyperparameters were selected on a training subset, and the run lasts 30 epochs.

rows.subject: UNet-like architecture with standard convolutions
rows.size_stated: Number of channels varied; exact tested values not stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied channel counts in the standard-convolution version of the architecture and plotted test error against parameter count.
rows.measure: Test error (1-MS-SSIM) as a function of parameter count
rows.note: The text says FLOP count grows steeply as generalization error decreases and that the curve flattens; it does not describe whether test error has a double-descent shape.
rows.check: The text says only that FLOPs grow very large 'before curve flattens'. It does not say whether a peak occurs. The Fig. 4 curve values cannot be read from the text.

relationships.condition: HyperConvolution UNet-like network on ZRR, nfwd=8, nembed=8, MLP hidden units varied, 30 epochs
relationships.reason: Authors state test error versus parameter count is consistent with double descent (R1). The support is qualitative and figure-only, with no peak location or training error.
relationships.display_finding: Test error varied with parameter count in a pattern consistent with double descent, without establishing the peak's relationship to training error.
